quote: Automatic Evaluation BLEU reflects the lexical overlap between the generated and the ground-truth text. BERTScore computes the similarity using contextual embeddings. ... We report the BLEU and BERTScore metrics for generated sentences compared against human written hyperboles.

We use the 71 literal sentences (para) in the test set of HYPO dataset as test inputs and their corresponding hyperbolic sentences (hypo) as gold references. We report the BLEU and BERTScore metrics for generated sentences compared against human written hyperboles.

We leverage the BERT-based hyperbole detection model fine‑tuned on HYPO and HYPO‑L to assign a hyperbole score (i.e., prediction probability) for each candidate. We also train a pairwise model (distilled RoBERTa‑base) to predict whether hyperbolic sentence A is a paraphrase of literal sentence B, providing a paraphrase score for ranking.

Human Evaluation ... We evaluate the generation results from the 71 testing literal sentences. Each pair of texts (ours vs. a baseline / human reference) is given preference (win, lose or tie) by five people with proficiency in English. We use a set of four criteria adapted from [citation] to evaluate the generated outputs: 1) Fluency (Flu.): Which sentence is more fluent and grammatical? 2) Hyperbolicity (Hypo.): Which sentence is more hyperbolic? 3) Creativity (Crea.): Which sentence is more creative? 4) Relevance (Rel.): Which sentence is more relevant to the input literal sentence?
